sanskrit: satyavān uvāca kāmaye darśanaṃ pitror yāhi sāvitri māciram purā mātuḥ pitur vāpi yadi paśyāmi vipriyam na jīviṣye varārohe satyenātmānam ālabhe
english: Satyavān said: I long to see my parents — go at once, Sāvitrī, do not delay. If I were to see any affliction of my mother or father, I could not live, O fair-limbed one; I swear this on my own soul by truth.

sanskrit: yadi dharme ca te buddhir māṃ cej jīvantam icchasi mama priyaṃ vā kartavyaṃ gacchasvāśramam antikāt
english: If your mind is set on dharma, and if you wish me to live, and if you desire to do what pleases me, then go now — leave at once for the hermitage nearby.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sāvitrī tata utthāya keśān saṃyamya bhāminī patim utthāpayām āsa bāhubhyāṃ parigṛhya vai
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then Sāvitrī rose, bound up her hair, and that devoted woman raised her husband, clasping him firmly with both arms.

sanskrit: utthāya satyavāṃś cāpi pramṛjyāṅgāni pāṇinā diśaḥ sarvāḥ samālokya kaṭhine dṛṣṭim ādadhe
english: Satyavān rose, wiped his limbs with his hand, surveyed all the directions, and then fixed his gaze upon the firewood bundle.

sanskrit: tam uvācātha sāvitrī śvaḥ phalānīha neṣyasi yogakṣemārtham etat te neṣyāmi paraśuṃ tv aham
english: Then Sāvitrī said to him: You shall carry the fruits tomorrow; for your welfare and support I will carry the axe for you now.

sanskrit: kṛtvā kaṭhinabhāraṃ sā vṛkṣaśākhāvalambinam gṛhītvā paraśuṃ bhartuḥ sakāśaṃ punar āgamat
english: Having placed the bundle of firewood hanging upon a tree branch, she took up the axe and came again to her husband's side.

sanskrit: vāme skandhe tu vāmorūr bhartur bāhuṃ niveśya sā dakṣiṇena pariṣvajya jagāma mṛdugāminī
english: The slender-thighed one laid her husband's arm upon her left shoulder, clasped him with her right arm, and walked on with gentle steps.

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca abhyāsagamanād bhīru panthāno viditā mama vṛkṣāntarālokitayā jyotsnayā cāpi lakṣaye
english: Satyavān said: O timid one, the paths are familiar to me from frequent travel; and by the moonlight filtering through the trees I can also make them out clearly.

sanskrit: āgatau svaḥ pathā yena phalāny avacitāni ca yathāgataṃ śubhe gaccha panthānaṃ mā vicāraya
english: Yesterday we came by a certain path and gathered fruits along it — O auspicious one, go back by the same road; do not waver from the path.

sanskrit: palāśaṣaṇḍe caitasmin panthā vyāvartate dvidhā tasyottareṇa yaḥ panthās tena gaccha tvarasva ca svastho 'smi balavān asmi didṛkṣuḥ pitarāv ubhau
english: In this grove of palāśa trees the path forks in two; take the northern branch and hurry along it — I am well, I am strong, and I am eager to see both my parents.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bruvann evaṃ tvarāyuktaḥ sa prāyād āśramaṃ prati
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Saying this and urging haste, he set out toward the hermitage.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu dyumatseno mahāvane labdhacakṣuḥ prasannātmā dṛṣṭyā sarvaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: At that very moment, Dyumatsena, in the great forest, had regained his sight; with a serene mind and clear vision he beheld all things around him.

sanskrit: sa sarvān āśramān gatvā śaibyayā saha bhāryayā putrahetoḥ parām ārtiṃ jagāma manujarṣabha
english: He went through all the hermitages with his wife Śaibya, and in his distress on account of his son he was overwhelmed with grief, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tāv āśramān nadīś caiva vanāni ca sarāṃsi ca tāṃs tān deśān vicinvantau dampatī parijagmatuḥ
english: The husband and wife wandered through hermitage after hermitage, river after river, forest after forest, and lake after lake, searching each region in turn.

sanskrit: śrutvā śabdaṃ tu yat kiṃ cid unmukhau sutaśaṅkayā sāvitrīsahito 'bhyeti satyavān ity adhāvatām
english: Hearing any sound at all and lifting their faces in hope that it was their son, they ran toward it — and indeed Satyavān approached together with Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: bhinnaiś ca paruṣaiḥ pādaiḥ savraṇaiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ kuśakaṣṭakaviddhāṅgāv unmattāv iva dhāvataḥ
english: With feet torn and rough, wounded and stained with blood, their bodies pierced by sharp kuśa grass and thorns, they ran like people driven mad.

sanskrit: tato 'bhisṛtya tair vipraiḥ sarvair āśramavāsibhiḥ parivārya samāśvāsya samānītau svam āśramam
english: Then all those brāhmaṇas dwelling in the hermitage came forward, surrounded the couple, comforted them, and brought them back to their own hermitage.

sanskrit: tatra bhāryāsahāyaḥ sa vṛto vṛddhais tapodhanaiḥ āśvāsito vicitrārthaiḥ pūrvarājñāṃ kathāśrayaiḥ
english: There, accompanied by his wife and surrounded by aged ascetics rich in penance, he was consoled with varied accounts drawing on the stories of kings of old.

sanskrit: tatas tau punar āśvastau vṛddhau putradidṛkṣayā bālye vṛttāni putrasya smarantau bhṛśaduḥkhitau
english: Then those two old ones, somewhat comforted yet longing to see their son, recalled the deeds of their son in childhood and were overcome with deep sorrow.

sanskrit: punar uktvā ca karuṇāṃ vācaṃ tau śokakarśitau hā putra hā sādhvi vadhūḥ kvāsi kvāsīty arodatām
english: Uttering pitiful words again, worn away by grief, they wept — "Alas, my son! Alas, virtuous daughter-in-law! Where are you, where are you?"

sanskrit: suvarcā uvāca yathāsya bhāryā sāvitrī tapasā ca damena ca ācāreṇa ca saṃyuktā tathā jīvati satyavān
english: Suvarcas said: As Sāvitrī, his wife, is endowed with austerity, self-restraint, and righteous conduct, so surely Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca vedāḥ sāṅgā mayādhītās tapo me saṃcitaṃ mahat kaumāraṃ brahmacaryaṃ me guravo 'gniś ca toṣitāḥ
english: Gautama said: I have studied the Vedas with all their auxiliary branches, I have accumulated great austerity, I observed celibacy from boyhood, and I have satisfied my teachers and the sacred fire.

sanskrit: samāhitena cīrṇāni sarvāṇy eva vratāni me vāyubhakṣopavāsaś ca kuśalāni ca yāni me
english: With concentrated mind I have observed all the vows, fasted living on air alone, and practised all the purifying disciplines that are mine.

sanskrit: anena tapasā vedmi sarvaṃ paricikīrṣitam satyam etan nibodha tvaṃ dhriyate satyavān iti
english: By this ascetic power I know all that has been done and all that is about to occur — know this for truth: Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: śiṣya uvāca upādhyāyasya me vaktrād yathā vākyaṃ viniḥsṛtam naitaj jātu bhaven mithyā tathā jīvati satyavān
english: The pupil said: As the word has gone forth from my teacher's mouth, it shall never prove false — thus Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ yathāsya bhāryā sāvitrī sarvair eva sulakṣaṇaiḥ avaidhavyakarair yuktā tathā jīvati satyavān
english: The sages said: As his wife Sāvitrī is endowed with all auspicious marks that ward off widowhood, so Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: bhāradvāja uvāca yathāsya bhāryā sāvitrī tapasā ca damena ca ācāreṇa ca saṃyuktā tathā jīvati satyavān
english: Bhāradvāja said: As his wife Sāvitrī is endowed with austerity, self-restraint, and righteous conduct, so Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: dālbhya uvāca yathā dṛṣṭiḥ pravṛttā te sāvitryāś ca yathā vratam gatāhāram akṛtvā ca tathā jīvati satyavān
english: Dālbhya said: As your sight has been restored to you, and as Sāvitrī's vow holds — she who went without food — so Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: māṇḍavya uvāca yathā vadanti śāntāyāṃ diśi vai mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ pārthivī ca pravṛttis te tathā jīvati satyavān
english: Māṇḍavya said: As the beasts and birds speak out in the peaceful direction, and as the earthly omens in your case are favourable, so Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: dhaumya uvāca sarvair guṇair upetas te yathā putro janapriyaḥ dīrghāyur lakṣaṇopetas tathā jīvati satyavān
english: Dhaumya said: As your son is endowed with all virtues, beloved of the people, long-lived, and bearing auspicious marks — so Satyavān lives.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evam āśvāsitas tais tu satyavāgbhis tapasvibhiḥ tāṃs tān vigaṇayann arthān avasthita ivābhavat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thus consoled by those truth-speaking ascetics, the king set aside anxiety after anxiety and became steady, as it were.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtāt sāvitrī bhartrā satyavatā saha ājagāmāśramaṃ rāttrau prahṛṣṭā praviveśa ha
english: Then after a short time Sāvitrī together with her husband Satyavān arrived, and at night she entered the hermitage full of joy.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ putreṇa saṃgataṃ tvādya cakṣuṣmantaṃ nirīkṣya ca sarve vayaṃ vai pṛcchāmo vṛddhiṃ te pṛthivīpate
english: The brāhmaṇas said: Having today seen you reunited with your son and having beheld you with sight restored, we all ask for your continued prosperity, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: samāgamena putrasya sāvitryā darśanena ca cakṣuṣaś cātmano lābhāt tribhir diṣṭyā vivardhase
english: By reunion with your son, by the sight of Sāvitrī, and by the recovery of your own eyes — by these three blessings you have fortunately prospered.

sanskrit: sarvair asmābhir uktaṃ yat tathā tan nātra saṃśayaḥ bhūyo bhūyaś ca vṛddhis te kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: What was said by all of us has come to pass — there is no doubt of it; and yet further and further prosperity shall quickly come to you.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato 'gniṃ tatra saṃjvālya dvijās te sarva eva hi upāsāṃ cakrire pārtha dyumatsenaṃ mahīpatim
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then those twice-born ones, kindling the sacred fire there, all paid homage to Dyumatsena, the great king, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: śaibyā ca satyavāṃś caiva sāvitrī caikataḥ sthitāḥ sarvais tair abhyanujñātā viśokāḥ samupāviśan
english: Śaibya, Satyavān, and Sāvitrī, having been granted permission by all of them, sat down together, free from sorrow.

sanskrit: tato rājñā sahāsīnāḥ sarve te vanavāsinaḥ jātakautūhalāḥ pārtha papracchur nṛpateḥ sutam
english: Then all those forest-dwellers, seated with the king and seized with curiosity, questioned the son of the king, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: prāg eva nāgataṃ kasmāt sabhāryeṇa tvayā vibho virātre cāgataṃ kasmāt ko 'nubandhaś ca te 'bhavat
english: Why did you not come earlier with your wife, O lord? And why did you come in the dead of night? What was the sequence of events for you?

sanskrit: saṃtāpitaḥ pitā mātā vayaṃ caiva nṛpātmaja nākasmād iti jānīmas tat sarvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: Your father, your mother, and all of us were tormented with grief, O son of the king — we know this did not happen without cause; please tell us everything.

sanskrit: satyavān uvāca pitrāham abhyanujñātaḥ sāvitrīsahito gataḥ atha me 'bhūc chiroduḥkhaṃ vane kāṣṭhāni bhindataḥ
english: Satyavān said: I was given leave by my father and went accompanied by Sāvitrī; then, while I was splitting wood in the forest, a pain arose in my head.

sanskrit: suptaś cāhaṃ vedanayā ciram ity upalakṣaye tāvat kālaṃ ca na mayā suptapūrvaṃ kadā cana
english: I lay down overcome by the pain and, as I reckon it, I slept for a long time — never before had I slept so long.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva bhavatāṃ saṃtāpo mā bhaved iti ato virātrāgamanaṃ nānyad astīha kāraṇam
english: I thought: may none of you all be made to suffer on my account — that is why I returned in the dead of night; there is no other reason for it.

sanskrit: gautama uvāca akasmāc cakṣuṣaḥ prāptir dyumatsenasya te pituḥ nāsya tvaṃ kāraṇaṃ vettha sāvitrī vaktum arhati
english: Gautama said: The recovery of sight by Dyumatsena your father was not without cause; you do not know the reason — Sāvitrī should speak of it.

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi sāvitri tvaṃ hi vettha parāvaram tvāṃ hi jānāmi sāvitri sāvitrīm iva tejasā
english: I wish to hear it, Sāvitrī — for you know the higher and the lower truth; I recognise you, Sāvitrī, as one equal in radiance to Sāvitrī herself.

sanskrit: tvam atra hetuṃ jānīṣe tasmāt satyaṃ nirucyatām rahasyaṃ yadi te nāsti kiṃ cid atra vadasva naḥ
english: You know the cause of all this — therefore let the truth be declared. If there is nothing secret in this, speak to us about it.

sanskrit: sāvitry uvāca evam etad yathā vettha saṃkalpo nānyathā hi vaḥ na ca kiṃ cid rahasyaṃ me śrūyatāṃ tathyam atra yat
english: Sāvitrī said: It is exactly as you suppose — your conviction is not otherwise. Nor is there anything secret on my part; hear what is true in this matter.

sanskrit: mṛtyur me bhartur ākhyāto nāradena mahātmanā sa cādya divasaḥ prāptas tato nainaṃ jahāmy aham
english: The death of my husband was foretold to me by the great-souled Nārada, and that very day had arrived — therefore I did not leave him.

sanskrit: suptaṃ cainaṃ yamaḥ sākṣād upāgacchat sakiṃkaraḥ sa enam anayad baddhvā diśaṃ pitṛniṣevitām
english: While he lay asleep, Yama himself came in person with his servants, bound him, and led him away toward the quarter frequented by the ancestors.

sanskrit: astauṣaṃ tam ahaṃ devaṃ satyena vacasā vibhum pañca vai tena me dattā varāḥ śṛṇuta tān mama
english: I praised that all-pervading god with truthful words, and by him five boons were granted to me — hear them from me.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī ca svarājyaṃ ca dvau varau śvaśurasya me labdhaṃ pituḥ putraśataṃ putrāṇām ātmanaḥ śatam
english: The restoration of sight and sovereignty — these two boons were for my father-in-law; for my father a hundred sons were obtained; and a hundred sons for myself.

sanskrit: caturvarṣaśatāyur me bhartā labdhaś ca satyavān bhartur hi jīvitārthaṃ tu mayā cīrṇaṃ sthiraṃ vratam
english: My husband Satyavān was obtained with a life of four hundred years; and it was for the life of my husband that I steadfastly observed the firm vow.

sanskrit: etat satyaṃ mayākhyātaṃ kāraṇaṃ vistareṇa vaḥ yathā vṛttaṃ sukhodarkam idaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahan mama
english: I have thus told you truly and in full the cause of all this — how this great sorrow of mine, as it unfolded, leads to happiness in the end.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ nimajjamānaṃ vyasanair abhidrutaṃ; kulaṃ narendrasya tamomaye hrade tvayā suśīle dhṛtadharmapuṇyayā; samuddhṛtaṃ sādhvi punaḥ kulīnayā
english: The sages said: The family of the king, which was sinking and beset by misfortunes, plunged in a dark lake of affliction, has been rescued by you, O woman of noble conduct, who hold to the merit of dharma — rescued once more by one who is truly of noble lineage.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tathā praśasya hy abhipūjya caiva te; varastriyaṃ tām ṛṣayaḥ samāgatāḥ narendram āmantrya saputram añjasā; śivena jagmur muditāḥ svam ālayam
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having thus praised and honoured that excellent woman, the assembled sages took proper leave of the king together with his son, and departed joyfully to their own dwellings by an auspicious road.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyām udite sūryamaṇḍale kṛtapūrvāhṇikāḥ sarve sameyus te tapodhanāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: When that night had passed and the sun's orb had risen, all those ascetics rich in penance gathered together, having completed their morning rites.

sanskrit: tad eva sarvaṃ sāvitryā mahābhāgyaṃ maharṣayaḥ dyumatsenāya nātṛpyan kathayantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Those great sages could not get their fill of narrating again and again to Dyumatsena all the great good fortune that had come through Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvāḥ śālvebhyo 'bhyāgatā nṛpa ācakhyur nihataṃ caiva svenāmātyena taṃ nṛpam
english: Then all the subjects who had come from the Śālva territories announced to the king that the king there had been slain by his own minister.

sanskrit: taṃ mantriṇā hataṃ śrutvā sasahāyaṃ sabāndhavam nyavedayan yathātattvaṃ vidrutaṃ ca dviṣadbalam
english: They reported truthfully that the minister had killed him along with his allies and kinsmen, and that the hostile army had been scattered and put to flight.

sanskrit: aikamatyaṃ ca sarvasya janasyātha nṛpaṃ prati sacakṣur vāpy acakṣur vā sa no rājā bhavatv iti
english: And they declared the unanimous will of all the people toward the king: "Whether he has sight or no sight, let him be our king."

sanskrit: anena niścayeneha vayaṃ prasthāpitā nṛpa prāptānīmāni yānāni caturaṅgaṃ ca te balam
english: "With this resolve we have been sent here, O king; these conveyances have arrived, and your fourfold army stands ready."

sanskrit: prayāhi rājan bhadraṃ te ghuṣṭas te nagare jayaḥ adhyāssva cirarātrāya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ padam
english: "Go forth, O king — blessings to you! Victory has been proclaimed in the city. Occupy for long years the ancestral throne inherited from your fathers and grandfathers."

sanskrit: cakṣuṣmantaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ vapuṣānvitam mūrdhabhiḥ patitāḥ sarve vismayotphullalocanāḥ
english: Beholding the king now with sight restored and possessed of his former handsome form, they all fell at his feet with wide eyes blooming in wonder.

sanskrit: tato 'bhivādya tān vṛddhān dvijān āśramavāsinaḥ taiś cābhipūjitaḥ sarvaiḥ prayayau nagaraṃ prati
english: Then, having reverenced those elder twice-born dwellers of the hermitage, and having been honoured by all of them in return, he set out toward the city.

sanskrit: śaibyā ca saha sāvitryā svāstīrṇena suvarcasā narayuktena yānena prayayau senayā vṛtā
english: Śaibya too set out together with Sāvitrī, upon a well-spread and richly decked conveyance drawn by men, surrounded by the army.

sanskrit: tato 'bhiṣiṣicuḥ prītyā dyumatsenaṃ purohitāḥ putraṃ cāsya mahātmānaṃ yauvarājye 'bhyaṣecayan
english: Then the royal chaplains joyfully consecrated Dyumatsena, and they consecrated his great-souled son in the position of crown prince.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena mahatā sāvitryāḥ kīrtivardhanam tad vai putraśataṃ jajñe śūrāṇām anivartinām
english: Then, in the course of time, that hundred sons who would enhance the fame of Sāvitrī were born — heroes who never turned back in battle.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇāṃ sodarāṇāṃ ca tathaivāsyābhavac chatam madrādhipasyāśvapater mālavyāṃ sumahābalam
english: And likewise there were born to Aśvapati, lord of the Madras, a hundred brothers of the same mother — of great might — from a Mālavī woman.

sanskrit: evam ātmā pitā mātā śvaśrūḥ śvaśura eva ca bhartuḥ kulaṃ ca sāvitryā sarvaṃ kṛcchrāt samuddhṛtam
english: Thus her own self, her father, her mother, her mother-in-law, her father-in-law, and the family of her husband — all were rescued from peril by Sāvitrī.

sanskrit: tathaivaiṣāpi kalyāṇī draupadī śīlasaṃmatā tārayiṣyati vaḥ sarvān sāvitrīva kulāṅganā
english: Even so shall this auspicious Draupadī, honoured for her character, like Sāvitrī a noble woman of her lineage, rescue all of you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sa pāṇḍavas tena anunīto mahātmanā viśoko vijvaro rājan kāmyake nyavasat tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus consoled by that great-souled one, the Pāṇḍava, free from grief and fever, dwelt at that time in Kāmyaka, O king.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca yat tat tadā mahābrahmaṃl lomaśo vākyam abravīt indrasya vacanād etya pāṇḍuputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Janamejaya said: What was the word that Lomaśa then spoke, O great brahmin, coming at Indra's bidding to Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu —

sanskrit: yac cāpi te bhayaṃ tīvraṃ na ca kīrtayase kva cit tac cāpy apahariṣyāmi savyasācāv ihāgate
english: "— and regarding that intense fear of yours which you disclose nowhere: 'that too I shall remove when the Left-handed Archer comes here' —

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tad viduṣāṃ śreṣṭha karṇaṃ prati mahad bhayam āsīn na ca sa dharmātmā kathayām āsa kasya cit
english: — what was that great fear regarding Karṇa, O best of the learned? And why did that righteous-souled one not speak of it to anyone?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ahaṃ te rājaśārdūla kathayāmi kathām imām pṛcchate bharataśreṣṭha śuśrūṣasva giraṃ mama
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: I shall tell you this tale, O tiger among kings, since you ask — O best of the Bhāratas, be attentive to my words.

sanskrit: dvādaśe samatikrānte varṣe prāpte trayodaśe pāṇḍūnāṃ hitakṛc chakraḥ karṇaṃ bhikṣitum udyataḥ
english: When the twelfth year had passed and the thirteenth arrived, Śakra, acting for the welfare of the Pāṇḍavas, set out to beg from Karṇa.

sanskrit: abhiprāyam atho jñātvā mahendrasya vibhāvasuḥ kuṇḍalārthe mahārāja sūryaḥ karṇam upāgamat
english: Then, having learned of Mahendra's intention, O great king, Vibhāvasu — the sun — approached Karṇa regarding the matter of the earrings.

sanskrit: mahārhe śayane vīraṃ spardhyāstaraṇasaṃvṛte śayānam abhiviśvastaṃ brahmaṇyaṃ satyavādinam
english: The hero lay on a most precious bed covered with a matchless spread, resting unsuspecting — devoted to the brahmins and ever truthful in speech.

sanskrit: svapnānte niśi rājendra darśayām āsa raśmivān kṛpayā parayāviṣṭaḥ putrasnehāc ca bhārata
english: At the end of a dream, in the night, O lord of kings, the radiant sun revealed himself, filled with the deepest compassion and moved by a father's love, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo vedavid bhūtvā sūryo yogād dhi rūpavān hitārtham abravīt karṇaṃ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: The sun, taking the form of a brahmin versed in the Vedas and possessed of a handsome form by his yogic power, spoke these soothing words to Karṇa for his benefit.
